summary: Nine concrete, comment-endorsed finds from the verified Hacker News front-page discussion crawl.
telegram_footer: 9 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Gander
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Gander, an Android file viewer that asks for no permissions
items.summary: An offline Android file viewer for documents, media, Markdown, and code.
items.why_included: A user independently praised its unusually quick PDF handling, while the project targets a real privacy and bloat problem.
items.evidence: One commenter said Gander was pleasingly responsive and unlike other Android apps for rapidly opening and closing PDFs.

evidence_sources.author: array4277
evidence_sources.excerpt: The app is pleasingly very responsive. I don't think I've used anything else on Android that lets me open and close PDFs rapidly without getting bogged down. Nice!

items.name: vLLM-Moet
items.source_story_title: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 Intelligence, Performance and Price Analysis
items.summary: A vLLM patch for running giant MoE models with compressed experts.
items.why_included: A hands-on commenter called it a very good engine and specifically recommended trying it for constrained high-memory GPUs.
items.evidence: The commenter reported a 170 tokens-per-second DeepSeek V4 Flash demonstration and recommended spending a few hours trying it.

evidence_sources.author: ycui7
evidence_sources.excerpt: vllm-moet is a very good engine, although lesser known.

items.name: Apache DataFusion
items.source_story_title: Algorithms on billion-scale graph using 10GB RAM: I love DataFusion
items.summary: A Rust and Arrow query engine for fast extensible data systems.
items.why_included: The discussion contained unusually strong, concrete praise for its design and extensibility.
items.evidence: A commenter called DataFusion one of the best open-source projects, highlighting its powerful design and ability to compile custom query languages into logical plans.

evidence_sources.author: nylonstrung
evidence_sources.excerpt: Datafusion is undoubtedly one of the best open source projects of all time, it's so incredibly powerful and well designed.

items.name: GraphChi
items.source_story_title: Algorithms on billion-scale graph using 10GB RAM: I love DataFusion
items.summary: A single-machine framework for large-scale graph computation.
items.why_included: It is a relevant, concrete alternative for large graph work that a commenter explicitly suggested exploring.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended GraphChi as another system designed for large-scale graph operations on one machine.

evidence_sources.author: cpdomina
evidence_sources.excerpt: you might be interested in graphchi (2012), also designed to do large scale graph operations on a single machine

items.name: jpeg2png
items.source_story_title: How JPEG works: Interactively explore JPEG's lossy compression methods
items.summary: A decoder that reconstructs a smoother image consistent with a JPEG.
items.why_included: A user tested it on badly compressed images and reported materially better results.
items.evidence: The commenter said they tried it on severely compressed images and found the outputs much better.

evidence_sources.author: netsharc
evidence_sources.excerpt: I tried it with some very terribly compressed images, and the outputs were a lot better.

items.name: Elevator Saga
items.summary: A programming game about writing elevator scheduling algorithms.
items.why_included: It was presented as an enjoyable rabbit hole and fits hands-on algorithmic learning.
items.evidence: A commenter introduced it as an elevator-scheduling game and encouraged readers to enjoy the rabbit hole.

evidence_sources.author: brandonpelfrey
evidence_sources.excerpt: For folks that have never seen elevator scheduling the game: https://play.elevatorsaga.com/ Enjoy this rabbit hole :D

items.name: The Intuitionist
items.summary: A speculative mystery novel about rival schools of elevator inspection.
items.why_included: It is an idiosyncratic book recommendation with a clearly enthusiastic, specific endorsement.
items.evidence: A commenter called it an amazing speculative mystery novel centered on two elevator-inspection philosophies.

evidence_sources.author: geephroh
evidence_sources.excerpt: Colson Whitehead's _The Intuitionist_[1], an amazing speculative mystery novel about two dueling schools of elevator inspection philosophies

items.name: Project Highrise
items.summary: A skyscraper construction and management simulation game.
items.why_included: A direct recommendation in a thread full of elevator-system enthusiasts makes it a useful adjacent find.
items.evidence: A commenter explicitly said Project Highrise was worth taking a look into for people who liked SimTower.

evidence_sources.author: Sohcahtoa82
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you liked SimTower, Project Highrise is worth taking a look into.
